name: pwnat
description: Proxy server that works behind a NAT

repo.name: pwnat
repo.description: The only tool/technique to punch holes through firewalls/NATs where multiple clients & server can be behind separate NATs without any 3rd party involvement. Pwnat is a newly developed technique, exploiting a property of NAT translation tables, with no 3rd party, port forwarding, DMZ, DNS, router admin requirements, STUN/TURN/UPnP/ICE, or spoofing.

readme.summary: Excellent explanation of what the tool does and how it works, but completely missing installation/build instructions.
readme.top_issue: No installation or build instructions - users don't know how to compile or install the binary before running './pwnat'

injection_risks.description: Potential buffer overflow vulnerability in sprintf function
Use of gethostbyname function which can lead to DNS spoofing attacks

critical_findings: Lack of input validation for command line arguments
security.summary: The code has several security concerns, including potential buffer overflow vulnerabilities and lack of input validation, which need to be addressed to ensure the security of the UDP tunnel server.

common_complaints: Windows compatibility issues (F_SETFL errors, build problems)
Poor documentation and unclear usage instructions
Lack of clarity on implementation principles
praise_themes: Tool concept is considered cool/innovative (NAT traversal approach)
sentiment.summary: pwnat shows signs of abandonment with unresponsive maintainers, 9 open issues spanning 2+ years without resolution, frequent build/compatibility problems, and poor documentation leaving users frustrated and confused about basic usage.

communication.summary: The maintainer provides detailed and technical responses, though there is room for more clarity in some points.

concerns: 21 open issues with no recent activity
No closed issues in past 6 months
No merged PRs in past 6 months
Zero active contributors in past 6 months
maintenance.summary: pwnat appears to be abandoned with no maintenance activity for at least 6 months and a growing backlog of unresolved issues.
